canonical_question: How does the 'adverse effect' of Mn-rich oxides specifically compare to the failure mechanisms observed in the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system at 1100 °C?

question_variants.question: How does the 'adverse effect' of Mn-rich oxides specifically compare to the failure mechanisms observed in the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system at 1100 °C?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text attributes the poor oxidation resistance of Mn-containing alloys to the 'adverse effect of Mn-rich oxides'. It does not explicitly describe the specific failure mechanisms in the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system to allow a direct comparison of the *nature* of the adverse effect, only the attribution of poor resistance.

answers.answer: The text states that the poor oxidation resistance of Mn-containing alloys is attributed to the 'adverse effect of Mn-rich oxides'. It does not provide details on the failure mechanisms of the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system to facilitate a specific comparison beyond this general attribution.
answers.mechanism: Attributed to the adverse effect of Mn-rich oxides.
answers.boundary_limitation: No specific failure mechanism details for Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system provided in the text.
evidence_spans: Nong et al. [12] studied the high temperature oxidation behavior of AlCrFeNiTiMn x (where x = 0 and 0.5) HEAs at 900 °C for 100 h and probed the poor oxidation resistance of Mn containing alloys, which was attributed to the adverse effect of Mn-rich oxides. The cumulative mass gain (CMG) of Mn-free and Mn-containing alloys was 6.9 mg/cm 2 and 8.7 mg/cm 2 , respectively.
